text: Ostriches can run faster than horses, reaching speeds up to 43 miles per hour (70 km/h).
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift away in ocean currents.
Octopuses have three hearts, nine brains, and blue blood based on copper instead of iron.
Honeybees can recognize and remember individual human faces.
Crows understand cause-and-effect reasoning and remember human faces for years.
Sloths can hold their breath underwater for up to 40 minutes, slowing their heart rate down to a third.
A group of flamingos gathered together is officially called a flamboyance.
Koalas have unique fingerprints that are virtually indistinguishable from human fingerprints.
Atlantic puffins mate for life and return to the exact same cliffside burrow year after year.
Elephants communicate over miles using infrasonic seismic vibrations detected through their padded feet.
A day on Venus (243 Earth days) lasts longer than an entire Venusian year (225 Earth days).
Neutron stars can spin up to 600 times per second, condensing twice the Sun's mass into the size of a city.
Over 1.3 million Earths could fit comfortably inside the volume of the Sun.
There is a giant interstellar molecular cloud near the center of the galaxy containing billions of liters of alcohol.
Sunsets on Mars appear distinctly blue because Martian atmospheric dust scatters red light away from the Sun.
Footprints left on the Moon by Apollo astronauts will stay intact for millions of years due to lack of wind and water erosion.
Saturn's rings are remarkably thin: though 175,000 miles wide, they are mostly only about 30 feet (10 meters) thick.
Jupiter has at least 95 confirmed moons orbiting around it, including Ganymede, which is larger than the planet Mercury.
Take a deep breath. Soften your jaw, drop your shoulders away from your ears, and release your brow.
Rest your eyes: look away from the display and focus on the furthest horizon or distant object you can see.
Hydrate: take a slow sip of cool water and feel the physical sensation as you pause before resuming.
Gently tilt your head toward each shoulder, feeling the stretch through your neck muscles.
Notice three sounds around you right now that you were tuning out moments ago.
Inhale slowly for four counts, pause gently for four, and exhale smoothly for six counts.
